description: Hand-authored questions over the tightly-scoped technical notes in this directory. Every line range was read back from the file and checked to contain the answer.

relevance_basis.location: A retrieved hit is relevant when its source_path matches a relevant_path AND its [start_line, end_line] range overlaps the corresponding relevant_line_range.
relevance_basis.chunk: A retrieved hit is relevant when its chunk_id is listed in relevant_chunk_ids. Those ids were read back from a real index built with the chunking config below; they are only valid for that configuration.
relevance_basis.graded: graded maps 'path:start-end' keys to an integer relevance grade used only by nDCG. Unlabelled gold locations default to grade 1.

notes: Paths are relative to this directory and are the same strings Orbit stores, because ingestion makes paths relative to the indexed root.

questions.question: When a fused ranking is displayed, how is a raw channel score rescaled into the unit interval?
questions.notes: Deliberately avoids the token min_max_normalize so the lexical channel cannot win on a rare identifier.

questions.question: What is the default value of rrf_k, and what does it stop from happening?
questions.notes: Exact rare identifier rrf_k. Appears in no other file.

questions.question: Which helper performs the rescaling, and what does it return when every score in the list is identical?
questions.notes: Targets min_max_normalize and its divide-by-zero guard.

questions.question: How is the full text index declared so that chunk text is not stored twice?
questions.notes: FTS5 external content over the chunks table.

questions.question: What is the transaction scope when a single document is indexed?
questions.notes: One transaction per document: chunk rows, FTS rows and embedding rows commit together.

questions.question: Does a citation that checks out prove that the retrieved claim is actually true?
questions.notes: Paraphrase of 'a citation is a pointer, not proof'.

questions.question: List the validation states a citation can be in.
questions.notes: Multi-line answer: VALID, CONTENT_CHANGED, PATH_MISSING, CHUNK_OUT_OF_RANGE, DOCUMENT_DELETED, NOT_VALIDATED.

questions.question: Which kinds of files are left out of the index because of what they are called?
questions.notes: Paraphrase of 'secret-like files are skipped'.

questions.question: How is a chunk identifier constructed, and why do two files with identical text get different identifiers?
questions.notes: document id (hash of path) joined to the chunk ordinal with a colon.

questions.question: What two inputs go into the per-chunk content hash?
questions.notes: Start line plus chunk text.

questions.question: Why can two ranking lists be merged without first putting their scores on a common scale?
questions.notes: RRF consumes ranks, not score magnitudes. No rare identifier appears in the question.

questions.question: What does the built-in hashing embedder guarantee, and what does it explicitly refuse to do?
questions.notes: Deterministic and offline, but not semantic.

questions.question: Which provider mean-pools token vectors, and what extra does it need installed?
questions.notes: The hf provider and the optional embeddings extra.

questions.question: How does a reindex avoid doing any work for a file that has not changed?
questions.notes: Paraphrase of the content-hash skip.

questions.question: How does vector search latency scale as the number of chunks grows?
questions.notes: Exact scan, linear in chunk count.

questions.question: Is a conflict candidate an explicit relation or an inferred one?
questions.notes: Inferred, never explicit.

questions.question: Which provenance fields must every MCP tool result carry?
questions.notes: Source path, line range and content hash.

questions.question: How are near-duplicate context blocks removed during assembly?
questions.notes: Identical content hash, plus a 0.92 similarity threshold.

questions.question: In what form does the command line print each search citation?
questions.notes: path:start-end, then score and retrieval method.

questions.question: Which kind of ground-truth label stays valid after the chunker is changed?
questions.notes: File plus line range, as opposed to a chunk identifier.
